facts.fact: obj.evaluated_get(depsgraph).data is the evaluated mesh (modifiers applied); obj.data stays the base mesh
evaluated.to_mesh() gives a temporary mesh not in bpy.data; release it with to_mesh_clear()
bpy.data.meshes.new_from_object(evaluated_obj) gives a real mesh datablock with modifiers applied (0 users until assigned)
new_from_object(original object) returns the BASE mesh without modifiers: pass the evaluated object
new_from_object accepts preserve_all_data_layers and depsgraph keywords
swapping obj.data for the new_from_object mesh and clearing the modifiers is an apply that needs no context
bpy.ops.object.modifier_apply(modifier=name) works headless without any override when the object is the active one
without an override, modifier_apply acts on the ACTIVE object, not the one you meant
with bpy.context.temp_override(object=ob, active_object=ob), modifier_apply applies on ob even when another object is active
the pre-3.2 style override (a context dict as the first positional argument) fails in 4.5
